tokens.v: A coaching session where the trainee drove a whole order-to-cash run himself: raise a sales order, let planning turn it into a planned order, turn that into a production order, issue the material, receive and inspect it, and ship it. Before any of that, the group spent twenty minutes changing one planning setting at a time and re-running the plan to watch what each change did — which turned out to be the most useful part of the recording.

topics.title: Why an order comes out bigger than the shortfall

tokens.v: The item needed 45 more units. It got an order for 50. That is not a bug — it is the order increment doing its job.

blocks.text: The item needed 45 more units. It got an order for 50. That is not a bug — it is the order increment doing its job.

tokens.v: What was shown:
Safety stock was 50 and there were 5 units on hand, so planning asked for 45.

items.text: Safety stock was 50 and there were 5 units on hand, so planning asked for 45.

tokens.v: The order increment was then changed from 1 to 25, meaning the item can only be ordered in blocks of 25.

items.text: The order increment was then changed from 1 to 25, meaning the item can only be ordered in blocks of 25.

tokens.v: Re-running the plan produced an order for 50 instead of 45 — the 5 units already in stock do not divide into a 25-unit block, so LN rounds the whole order up to the next clean multiple.

items.text: Re-running the plan produced an order for 50 instead of 45 — the 5 units already in stock do not divide into a 25-unit block, so LN rounds the whole order up to the next clean multiple.

topics.title: Safety stock is a kind of demand

tokens.v: Safety stock is not just a floor that gets watched. Planning treats it as a demand in its own right, the same way it treats a sales order.

blocks.text: Safety stock is not just a floor that gets watched. Planning treats it as a demand in its own right, the same way it treats a sales order.

tokens.v: What was shown:
Drop below your safety stock and planning raises an order to top you back up, with nothing else asking for the item.

items.text: Drop below your safety stock and planning raises an order to top you back up, with nothing else asking for the item.

tokens.v: Set safety stock to zero with no orders outstanding, and a planning run correctly produces nothing at all — there is simply nothing asking for the item.

items.text: Set safety stock to zero with no orders outstanding, and a planning run correctly produces nothing at all — there is simply nothing asking for the item.

tokens.v: The three things that can ask for an item, in the consultant's own list: safety stock, a production order that needs it as a component, and a sales order.
